witness.text:
What if I told you that turning 30 in
the year 2030 might cost you more than
buying a house did for your parents?

comparisons.rationale: A concrete, generational what-if question with an immediate exaggeration ("financial gymnastics ... Olympic athlete weep") that works as a stop beat.
comparisons.uncertainty: Inferred from text and title/thumbnail only; no retention, click or viewer data exists, so this is a design judgment, not measured behaviour.

witness.text:
grocery and dining costs are
expected to rise by approximately 26%
by 2030

comparisons.rationale: Stated alongside "an average annual inflation rate of over 2%", which compounds to about 10% over five years; 26% requires about 4.7% a year, so the figure and its stated basis disagree (the $250 to over $300 example matches the 26%, not the 2%).
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

witness.text:
A four-year degree from a
public university could cost over
$200,000
total by 2030

comparisons.rationale: Four years at the stated $44,000 is $176,000, not over $200,000 (the total may include room and board, which the video does not say); and $44,000 a year is far above current in-state public tuition and fees (about $11,000-$12,000) and above typical in-state cost of attendance (about $29,000), though out-of-state costs approach $49,000; the video does not say which public college.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified; current College Board levels are analyst recall.

witness.text:
A student earning minimum wage would
need to work 40 hours per week just to
cover tuition and room and board

comparisons.rationale: At the federal minimum of $7.25 an hour, 40 hours a week for 52 weeks earns about $15,100, so it could not cover $44,000; the claim understates the problem and contradicts its own figure.
comparisons.uncertainty: Arithmetic verified.

financial_checks.claim: Grocery and dining costs rise 26% by 2030 with annual inflation "over 2%"
Public college $44,000 a year; four years "over $200,000"
Minimum-wage student working 40 hours a week covers tuition and room and board
financial_checks.result: $7.25 x 2,080 hours = $15,080 a year; cannot cover $44,000.
$162,170. Holds (assumption differs from the 3% and 2% used elsewhere in the video).

financial_checks.claim: Healthcare +20% by 2030: $5,000 to $6,000; costs double "approximately every nine years" at 7-8%
financial_checks.result: $6,000 is +20%; doubling at 7-8% takes 9-10 years. But the video's own "7 to 8% annually" is about +40-47% over five years, not +20%.

financial_checks.claim: Housing $382,000 average by 2030; ownership cost "approaching $4,000 a month"
financial_checks.result: About $3,300-$3,600 a month under common 5-10% down, 7% assumptions.

financial_checks.claim: Real wages down 7.6% since 2006; millennial average salary $71,000; 55% of Gen Z and millennials run side hustles earning $13,000-$18,000; Medicare +7.2% a year; car-ownership costs +43% since 2019; insurance +19% year over year; EV repair $6,600; childcare $25,000-$35,000 by 2030; retirement healthcare $350,000-$400,000
financial_checks.result: Not verified; none is sourced in the video. The childcare and real-wage figures appear inconsistent with national series as recalled; the healthcare estimate resembles Fidelity's couple figure.

strengths: Strong hook and a clear date-anchored premise.
Correct compounding where it is computed ($162,000, doubling time).
weaknesses: The headline promise (the income needed at 30 in 2030) is never computed.
Several figures contradict their own stated basis (26%, $200,000, minimum wage).
Subscribe ask before value and no actionable ending.

Hyperbole without support: "houses cost more than their lifetime earnings", "moving costs more than most people earn annually", "childcare already exceeds college tuition in most states" (not assessed here).
contradictions: 2% inflation versus a 26% food-price rise by 2030.
$44,000 a year versus "over $200,000" for four years.
A $382,000 projected 2030 home price versus higher 2026 medians stated by the same channel.
Three inflation rates (2%, 3%, 4%) in one video.
Healthcare "+20% by 2030" (about 3.7% a year) versus "7 to 8% annually" (about +44% over five years).
improvement_opportunities: Add one on-screen table totalling the 2030 categories into a required annual income and say what share of earners clear it.
Align inflation assumptions (state one rate) and recompute the food, tuition and housing lines.
Name sources on screen for each projection and drop the unsourced ones.
Close with a three-step plan and a next-video pointer; move the subscribe ask after the first data section.
